item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports attribute-sensitive representations, but the closest papers do not establish the exact from-scratch setup requested. [MARS (CIKM 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00702) learns multiple attribute-aware user/item representations and matches them attribute-wise, offering a mechanism for distinguishing detailed preferences beyond overall textual similarity. Its text-based approach uses pretrained language models. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) incorporates titles, descriptions and reviews through BERT; pretrained weights and review inputs make it unsuitable for direct adoption here. Neither establishes physical product compatibility from titles/descriptions alone.\n\nNegative sampling provides a more transferable direction. [ASRM++ (2025)](https://ecmlpkdd-storage.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/preprints/2025/ads/preprint_ecml_pkdd_2025_ads_116.pdf) samples negatives sold in the target’s month to align training with auction availability; that protocol is domain-specific and should not change the pinned Amazon evaluation. [Context-Aware Negative Sampling (2025)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/11021640) reports improved diversity with a small accuracy loss, so harder/contextual negatives do not guarantee higher HR@10. A constraint-compatible hypothesis—not a verified result—is to jointly train a small token-embedding pooling encoder with item IDs inside the existing HSTU, preserving model numbers, units and connector terms from supplied text. Mix uniform negatives with text-near items differing in explicit attributes, excluding known training positives. Keep one jointly trained score and checkpoint per category; treat compatibility inferred from text as uncertain, and select the sampling mix solely through macro validation HR@10."}
